_comment: Spec for scripts/soul-section-author.py. Copy and edit to author another fleet-wide SOUL section. `core` is the shared body; %s is where the per-profile `patterns` block lands. `patterns` keys are SOUL folder names for the source tree (lowercased, spaces->underscores) and profile ids for the loaded mirrors; '_default' is the fallback. `subsections`/`forbids` drive --verify.
label: card-handoff
heading: ## Inter-Profile Card Handoff
subsections: When to create a card for another profile
When to split the work into two or more cards
core:
%s

### Rule
- The kanban card is the only channel for cross-profile work. Never use the Hermes API server or a direct profile invocation to hand a task to another profile.
- One card carries one owner and one expected outcome. A single request may need two or more cards when it spans two or more profiles — you are expected to create as many as the work requires.
- If the room has no kanban board yet, create one before writing the card.

### When to create a card for another profile
1. The request, decision, or finding belongs to another profile's domain — assign by role fit, not by convenience.
2. The item is important, blocking, or time-critical for another profile's work and you cannot close it yourself.
3. A decision or instruction you received changes scope, sequence, priority, or acceptance criteria that another profile owns.
4. You completed part of the work and the remainder needs a different owner — open a follow-up card instead of leaving a comment.
5. The input is ambiguous and the intended outcome cannot be inferred — assign it to `not_known_task` and record what is missing.
6. The work is recurring or scheduled — tag the card as `cron` and route execution to the proper non-cron owner.
7. It is a room/project lifecycle change (create/delete) — include a linked `knowledge` card so the OV structure stays aligned.
8. You are blocking someone else's progress and their owner needs to know — raise the card instead of waiting to be asked.

### When to split the work into two or more cards
1. Two or more profiles own different parts of the same request — create one card per profile; never put two owners on one card.
2. There is primary work and supporting work — one primary card for the owning profile, plus a supporting card for each other profile that must act.
3. One part must wait for another — still create the dependent card, and state in it which card gates it, instead of holding the dependency privately.
4. One part changes shared structure or documentation — create the linked `knowledge` card alongside the main card so OV and knowledge records stay aligned.
5. A follow-up must happen after the current work settles — create the follow-up card now, marked as gated on the card(s) it depends on.
6. The same item fans out to several recipients — create one card per recipient profile, or one card per group of identical work.

### Multi-card rules
- One card, one owner. If a card would need two assignees, split it into two cards.
- Every card must stand alone: verbatim original text, target profile, reason, expected outcome, status, room and project context.
- Cross-reference the sibling cards in each card body (naming what the other cards cover) so the set stays traceable.
- Do not create two cards for the same work with the same owner and the same expected outcome.
- Do not use one card as a broadcast channel for several profiles — that is what the split is for.
- Keep, at most, the card you actually own; every other card must be assigned and handed off.

### Every handoff card must contain
- the original request or message text, verbatim
- the target profile
- the delegation reason (why that profile)
- the expected outcome or acceptance criteria
- the current status
- the room and project context

### Guardrails
- Do not create a card for work you can complete yourself in this session.
- Do not create cards for purely informational notes — those belong in the room or OV, not on the board.
- Do not leave a card without an owner, a reason, or acceptance criteria.
- Do not keep ownership of a card you have delegated — update the status, then hand it off.
- Do not use `add_project_todo` / `edit_project_todo` as a substitute for cross-profile handoff; the card is the handoff channel.

### Your typical handoff patterns
%s

default: Any request that needs a specialist profile and is not plain chat: write the card and assign it to that profile.
If this room has no board yet, create it before writing the first card.
If the request spans several profiles, create one card per profile rather than one card with several owners.
Intent that cannot be inferred goes to `not_known_task`.
action: Evidence or research is needed before delivery -> `market_research`.
Shared knowledge structure or documentation must change -> `knowledge`.
The item is planning/sequencing rather than execution -> `company_project` or `project_manager`.
If two of those apply at once, create both cards — do not stack two owners on one card.
ask_from_w: The user asks for a change, not an answer -> `delegator` for routing, or `action` when the work is already approved.
Deep analysis or market evidence is requested -> `business_analyst` or `market_research`.
Never raise a card only to inform another profile; this profile answers questions and stays read-only by default.
business_analyst: Ownership and sequencing of the resulting plan -> `company_project` or `project_manager`.
A plan that needs both execution and documentation becomes two cards, not one shared card.
coder: A decision you received changes scope, sequence, priority, or acceptance criteria -> `project_manager`, `company_project`, or `business_analyst` as owner.
New shared knowledge structure is needed -> `knowledge`.
The requirement or spec is missing or ambiguous -> `business_analyst`; if intent itself is unclear -> `not_known_task`.
The remainder of the work is non-code delivery -> `action`.
If a decision also changes knowledge structure, create the `knowledge` card in addition to the owning profile's card.
company: If one item needs both a project owner and a knowledge update, create both cards.
company_project: Schedule-based work -> tag the card `cron` and route to the proper non-cron owner.
If a card needs another profile's support, raise the supporting card instead of widening the first card's owner.
config: Execution that follows from a config change -> hand back through `delegator`.
A config change needs a profile-side follow-up (soul, tool, skill, MCP) -> card for that profile.
Several profiles are affected -> one card per affected profile.
Never apply a cross-profile change without an explicit card naming the target.
cron_profile: Cron or recurring card validated -> reassign to the proper non-cron owner (`action`, `knowledge`, `company_project`, `company`) with recurrence metadata.
Classification is done and execution ownership must leave this profile.
If the recurring work also needs a knowledge record, create the additional `knowledge` card for it.
delegator: Every non-explicit message must become a card before delegation.
Unclear input -> `not_known_task` with what is missing.
Recurring input -> cron tag plus non-cron execution owner.
Primary owner plus an OV/knowledge update means two cards (primary card and the linked `knowledge` card), not one merged card.
A mixed-intent request gets one card per dominant intent owner, each cross-referenced to the others.
knowledge: An artifact implies code or implementation change -> `action`.
A knowledge change has planning or sequencing consequences -> `company_project` or `project_manager`.
If the artifact change also needs implementation, create the `action` card alongside your own work.
market_research: Research output must be filed as project knowledge or an ADR -> `knowledge`.
Findings imply requirement or scope changes -> `business_analyst`.
If findings drive both a requirement change and execution, create both cards.
mechanical-modeler: The modeler itself (its code or MCP server) must change -> `coder`.
Model artifacts must be documented or published -> `knowledge`.
The request is W-space company/project work rather than modeling -> `company_project` or `action`, and `not_known_task` when unclear.
If a change needs both code and documentation, create both cards.
normal_message: If the capture exposes two different owners, create one card for each.
Never send a direct room reply; the OV entry plus the handoff card is the delivery.
not_known_task: After triage, reassign to the best-fit profile with a short rationale.
If triage reveals two distinct owners, split the card into one card per owner and reassign both.
Keep the original user message verbatim and add triage notes separately.
project_manager: Distribute WBS items by role fit to `business_analyst`, `market_research`, `coder`, `knowledge`, `action`, or `normal_message`.
Cron-tagged items -> the proper non-cron execution owner.
When one WBS item spans two profiles, create one card per profile rather than one card with two owners.
testprofile: Any work that belongs to another profile -> write the card and assign it.
Work spanning several profiles -> one card per profile.
_default: Anything that belongs to another profile's domain -> write the card and assign it.
Work spanning several profiles -> one card per profile.
